title: Investigate safe dynamic-state access in YAML score templates
description:
Investigate the generic LangGraph/Jinja rendering boundary using repository code, sanitized fixtures, synthetic experiments, Git history, and primary upstream sources.

Deliverable: document required template capabilities, exposed data types and trust boundaries, behavior of the restricted environment, risks of a global unrestricted-environment override, and a recommended supported design with alternatives.

Constraints: no production fix, no production configuration inspection or edits, no client information, and no deployment activity.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Investigation started. Scope is restricted to generic repository code, sanitized fixtures, synthetic data, history, and primary upstream sources. An isolated worktree will be created from origin/develop; no production configuration inspection or production change is authorized.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text:
## Final investigation findings

### Observations
- Repository prompt nodes create LangChain Jinja chat prompts from configured system/user message fields and render them with a dumped graph state. The normal state is mostly dictionaries, lists, and scalars; the schema permits extra values, so a rendering boundary must not assume every value is JSON-like.
- The current import-time workaround globally replaces LangChain Core 0.3.81’s restricted sandbox with plain Jinja `Environment` plus `ChainableUndefined`. This restores dotted mapping traversal and permits arbitrary Python-object attribute access and callable execution.
- LangChain Core 0.3.81 blocks every attribute access and callable to prevent template injection through object methods. It still permits dictionary bracket lookup.
- Sanitized repository tests demonstrate dotted mapping access. Code comments document a nested mapping plus bracket lookup requirement. No inspected sanitized test demonstrated loops, filters, or conditionals.

### Synthetic probe (Python 3.11; LangChain Core 0.3.81; Jinja 3.1.6)
- Restricted environment: bracket lookup passed; dotted mapping access and a dotted conditional failed with `SecurityError`.
- Plain environment: dotted access, conditionals, loops, and filters passed, but synthetic object dunder access and a synthetic method call also passed.
- Mapping-only sandbox prototype: dotted access, bracket lookup, conditional, loop, and `upper` filter passed; synthetic dunder access rendered empty and synthetic method call was blocked.

### Recommended direction
Do not keep the global private-symbol monkeypatch. Create a Plexus-owned rendering boundary that first recursively normalizes graph state to JSON-like mappings/lists/scalars, then renders through a narrowly customized `SandboxedEnvironment`. Its dot access should mean mapping-key lookup only; deny underscore-prefixed keys/attributes, every callable, and all non-JSON-like object access. Preserve `ChainableUndefined` only if missing-value behavior is a compatibility requirement. Inject only explicitly reviewed filters/globals.

### Alternatives and tradeoffs
1. Custom mapping-only sandbox: no ordinary template changes; moderate compatibility risk for templates that rely on object attributes; strongest practical compatibility/security balance; add synthetic capability and negative-security tests.
2. Recursive JSON-like conversion plus the custom sandbox: no template changes for mapping/list/scalar access; may expose latent non-serializable state dependencies; substantially reduces object surface; validate state shape before rendering.
3. Explicit lookup filters/functions: requires template migration; smallest implicit surface; higher migration burden; use for new templates or a long-term stricter DSL.
4. Supported upstream extension point: best maintenance outcome if LangChain/Tactus supplies one; requires upstream API/design and version migration; do not depend on a private monkeypatch.

### Migration/testing
Characterize all repository-owned templates with a sanitized AST/capability inventory, add fixtures for nested mapping, indexing, missing values, conditionals, loops, filters, dunder/method denial, and non-JSON state rejection; ship behind an opt-in renderer, compare rendered output on sanitized fixtures, then remove the global override.

### Primary sources
- https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/langchain-core%3D%3D0.3.81/libs/core/langchain_core/prompts/string.py
- https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/commit/fa7789d6c21222b85211755d822ef698d3b34e00
- https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/3.1.x/sandbox/

### Remaining questions
- Are repository template sources strictly reviewed/versioned, or can an untrusted actor influence them?
- Which non-JSON values may reach `extra` graph state in real workflows?
- Is silent chainable-undefined behavior required, or should absent paths become visible validation errors?
